Reference notes for **Math 165: Calculus I** at the
[University of North Dakota](https://und.edu/academics/online/enroll-anytime/math165.html),
which I'm taking to build a solid math foundation for computer science, machine
learning, and AI. Derivatives in particular are everywhere in machine learning:
gradient descent and backpropagation are built on them.

These pages collect the **definitions, theorems, and key ideas** I want to
memorize and look up later, retyped from the course textbook with its numbering
kept, so each box can be matched with the book.

## Topics in this module

- **[Chapter 1 — Limits](limits/index.qmd)** — the ε–δ definition, limit laws and
  special limits, one-sided and infinite limits, asymptotes, and continuity
  (§1.0–1.6).
- **[Chapter 2 — Derivatives](derivatives/index.qmd)** — the derivative and its
  notation, differentiation rules, higher-order derivatives, and the chain rule
  (§2.0–2.6 so far).
- **[Quick reference](quick-reference/index.qmd)** — limit laws, special limits,
  continuity, and derivative rules on one page.
- *Chapter 3 — The Graphical Behavior of Functions (extreme values, the Mean
  Value Theorem, curve sketching)* — planned.
- *Chapters 4–5 — Applications of derivatives, and integration* — planned.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Items marked *planned* are placeholders for notes I'll add as I work through the
course.
:::
